comentarios.texto: Saving the notification level directly leaves notifications_reason_id unchanged instead of recording an explicit user choice. For automatically tracked topics with a null reason, TopicUser.update_last_read promotes the row back to tracking when the reading threshold is exceeded, undoing the unsubscribe on the next read. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at are set consistently with set_notifications.

Saving the notification level directly bypasses the explicit-user-change metadata set by TopicUser.change. In particular, a topic_user with notifications_reason_id == nil remains eligible for TopicUser.auto_track, which checks that field and can promote the topic back to tracking after the user unsubscribes. Use the notification-change helper (or set its user-change reason and timestamp consistently) so the unsubscribe is retained as an explicit user preference.

issues.descricao: Claims the client unsubscribe route never performs the unsubscribe when entered through an in-app transition.

comentarios.texto: The client unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view and never performs the unsubscribe operation. When entered through an in-app transition rather than a full server navigation, PostStream.loadTopicView requests /t/:id.json (or consumes preload data), so the page claims notifications will stop while the persisted notification level remains unchanged. Ensure this entry path executes the unsubscribe operation before showing confirmation.

The client route loads the topic but never invokes the unsubscribe action. Notification levels are changed only by TopicsController#unsubscribe, so navigating to this route inside the Ember application can display “You will stop receiving notifications” without changing the subscription. Explicitly perform the unsubscribe operation on client-side entry rather than relying on the initial HTML request to have done it.

issues.descricao: The property name stopNotificiationsText is misspelled (should be stopNotificationsText).
issues.textoGolden: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

issues.descricao: The topic unsubscribe GET endpoint is not idempotent: each visit steps the notification level down again, so reloading the link moves a topic from regular to muted.

sugestoes.texto: Anonymous requests for TL0 profiles now receive `website_name` even though `restrict_user_fields?` suppresses `website`, exposing the restricted website hostname and, for matching domains, its path through the public user endpoint. Add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` so it uses the same visibility predicate as `website`.

issues.descricao: website_name compares hostnames case-sensitively, so an uppercase website host matching the instance domain shows only the host instead of the full path.

comentarios.texto: The new `website_name` compares two domain names case-sensitively. `URI(website.to_s).host` preserves the letter case written by the user, whereas `Discourse.current_hostname` is the canonical lower-cased host, and no side is down-cased before the comparison at lines 141, 144-146 and 149 (including the `ends_with?` suffix check). Because DNS host names are case-insensitive identity values, `http://EXAMPLE.com/user` and `http://example.com/user` denote the same host but take different branches, so the same-site check is decided by letter case: the wrong arm is chosen and the full-path form is dropped. Normalise both sides before comparing, e.g. `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host&.downcase` (or use `URI(...).hostname`, which down-cases) and compare against `Discourse.current_hostname.to_s.downcase`.

Hostname comparisons are case-sensitive even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive. With an instance hostname of example.com and a valid website of http://EXAMPLE.COM/user, neither the exact-host nor suffix comparison matches, so the profile displays only EXAMPLE.COM instead of the requested path. Normalize both hostnames to lowercase for comparison while preserving the desired display spelling.

issues.descricao: website_name strips only the first label to decide same-domain, so unrelated hosts under multi-label public suffixes (co.uk, github.io) are treated as the instance domain and shown with full path.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the `elsif` branch treats the last two dot-segments as the registrable domain, so multi-part public suffixes are mis-compared. WHY: for e.g. website_host='example.co.uk' and discourse_host='forum.co.uk' both have 3 segments, the branch compares `'co.uk' == 'co.uk'`, concludes the domains match, and returns `website_host + path`, even though example.co.uk and forum.co.uk are unrelated sites — the display then shows a path that does not belong to the instance domain, defeating the feature's purpose. HOW: compare against a public-suffix-aware registrable domain (e.g. use the PublicSuffix list) or require at least the full suffix before treating hosts as the same domain, instead of blindly taking `split('.')[1..-1]`.

Comparing all labels except the first incorrectly treats unrelated domains under multi-label public suffixes as the same domain. For example, with instance host `forum.co.uk` and website `https://unrelated.co.uk/user`, this returns `unrelated.co.uk/user` rather than the unrelated-site host-only label. Both hosts have three labels and their suffixes are `co.uk`, so this branch mistakes the public suffix for a shared site domain. Use registrable-domain-aware comparison (or a narrower explicit host relationship) before including the path.

The same-label-count branch treats two hosts as the same domain when everything after the first label matches. Unrelated hosts on shared suffixes, such as `a.github.io` and `b.github.io`, are treated as the same domain, so the full path is shown for an unrelated website. Compare against the registrable domain, for example with the PublicSuffix gem, or drop this heuristic branch.

issues.descricao: Claims website_name should also show the full path when the website is a subdomain of the instance host.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Else branch only tests `discourse_host.ends_with?('.'+website_host)` (discourse child of website) and misses the reverse (website subdomain of instance). WHY: With instance `example.com` and website `http://sub.example.com/page`, it returns `sub.example.com` instead of `sub.example.com/page`, contradicting the PR intent to show the full path for same-base-domain URLs. HOW: Also return host+path when `website_host` ends with `.`+discourse_host or shares the same registrable domain.

issues.descricao: website_name is not marked untrusted, so the host/path of a TL0 user's website, which is hidden from anonymous viewers, is still exposed through the new field.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: website_name re-exposes the user's website for profiles where it is intentionally hidden — the attribute is added to the public `attributes` list (line 43) but not to `untrusted_attributes`, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` instead of `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. WHY: `website` is an untrusted attribute gated by `restrict_user_fields?` (lib/guardian/user_guardian.rb:58-60), which is true for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous visitor; `website_name` derives `website_host + path` from the same `object.user_profile.website`, so the URL that `include_website?` suppresses is still disclosed through the new key (the existing spec at spec/serializers/user_serializer_spec.rb:11-14 only asserts the listed untrusted keys are absent, so this leak is not covered). HOW: add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (or have `include_website_name` return false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`), mirroring the `website` handling.

`website_name` is derived from the same `object.user_profile.website` value that `:website` protects via `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111), but it is only gated by `include_website_name` -> `website.present?`. Since the untrusted filter removes `website` for some viewers while `website_name` is still emitted, and in the same-domain / subdomain branches it returns host *plus* `URI(website).path` (lines 143/146/149), the user's full website URL still leaves in the response for viewers the filter was supposed to strip it from. Either add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or gate `include_website_name` with the same trust condition as `website`.

The new `website_name` field is gated only on `website.present?`, ignoring the visibility constraint this file declares for its source attribute: lines 105-111 put `:website` in `untrusted_attributes`, so `website` is omitted for viewers not allowed to see profile fields, but `website_name` is still serialized because `include_website_name` never consults that condition. Those viewers now receive the user's URL host, and when the host equals (lines 141-143) or is a parent of (144-149) the instance host they receive host + path, i.e. the complete URL that `website` was supposed to hide. Fix by adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (105-111) — or make the guard reuse `website`'s own inclusion condition instead of a bare presence check.

issues.descricao: include_website_name lacks the '?' suffix that ActiveModelSerializers requires, so the conditional-inclusion guard is never called.
issues.textoGolden: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` required by ActiveModelSerializers. WHY: every other conditional-inclusion guard in this file uses the `?` form (`define_method "include_#{attr}?"` at lines 9/18/27, `include_email?` at line 117), and AMS 0.8.3 resolves the guard as `include_<attr>?`; because this method lacks the `?` it is never invoked, so the intended `website.present?` condition is silently ignored and `website_name` is always serialized. HOW: rename to `def include_website_name?`.

The guard method is named `include_website_name`, but ActiveModelSerializers (and this file's own convention, e.g. `include_email?` at line 117) resolves per-attribute guards via `include_<attribute>?`. Because the name lacks the trailing `?`, the framework never invokes it: the `website.present?` guard is dead code and `website_name` is serialized unconditionally, emitting `website_name: null` for users without a website. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

The conditional-inclusion guard is named `include_website_name`, but ActiveModelSerializers resolves these guards as `include_<attribute>?` (the sibling in this very file is `include_email?` at line 117). As written the method is never called, so the guard is dead and the `:website_name` attribute declared at line 43 is serialized unconditionally. That defeats the intent of the guard (`website.present?`): the payload now always carries `website_name`, including for the scopes where `website` itself is withheld by the `untrusted_attributes` list (line 109), leaking the user's site host/path to viewers who were never meant to receive the website. Rename the method to `include_website_name?` so the serializer base class honors it.

issues.descricao: UserSerializer#website_name re-parses URI(website.to_s) for the path after already parsing it for the host instead of reusing one parsed URI.

sugestoes.texto: When a user already has locally stored recovery codes and regeneration succeeds in user storage, this branch leaves the previous local credential active; `UserCredentialManager.isValid` falls back to the local recovery provider when external validation rejects an old code. Remove existing locally stored recovery credentials after successfully replacing them in user storage so regeneration invalidates the previous set.

A successful recovery-code check never removes the matching code, and `getCredentials` reconstructs the complete original set on every lookup, so the same code authenticates indefinitely and the UI always requests code 1. Persist consumption on successful validation and return the remaining-code state rather than rebuilding an unused set.

issues.descricao: The test user-storage provider validates recovery codes without consuming the used code, so the same code can be replayed.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new recovery-codes branch of isValid only checks whether the submitted code appears in the stored list and never removes the consumed entry. WHY: Unlike the local RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.isValid (which calls removeRecoveryAuthnCode()+updateStoredCredential), the federated path never consumes a code and allCodesUsed() can never become true, so a used recovery code remains valid and can be replayed indefinitely. HOW: On a successful match, remove that entry from the stored codes (rewrite recoveryCodes.credentialData), mirroring the local provider's consume-on-success semantics.

The new recovery-code validator accepts any code in the original list without consuming the accepted code. Repeating a successful login with the same code succeeds indefinitely, while getCredentials reconstructs all original codes so the login form never advances or detects exhaustion. Validate the next unused code and persist its consumption before returning success.

The new federated recovery-code validator accepts any code in the original list but never removes a successfully used code from myUser.recoveryCodes. Consequently the same recovery code remains valid on subsequent logins, and getCredentials reconstructs the full original set every time. Consume and persist the successfully validated code (and test a second login/replay), so federated recovery codes retain their one-time semantics.

issues.descricao: getCredentials rebuilds the recovery-codes credential without copying the stored credential id, so the returned federated credential has a null id and cannot be targeted by id-based removal.
issues.textoGolden: After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getCredentials builds the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues but never sets its id from the stored myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() (createFromValues does not populate id). WHY: The returned federated model has a null id, so callers that identify/delete the credential by id — e.g. RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) when all codes are used, or federated-credential deletion via getFederatedCredentialsStream — cannot target the actual credential. HOW: call model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()) after createFromValues.

getCredentials rebuilds the recovery-code model without copying the ID assigned during updateCredential. createFromValues does not assign an ID, so the exposed federated credential has a null ID and CredentialDeleteHelper cannot resolve it by the stored credential ID for account deletion. Copy myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() to the reconstructed model before returning it.

The CredentialModel returned from getCredentials for recovery codes is built with createFromValues and never gets the stored credential's id (myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()). RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator later calls removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId()) once all codes are used, and this would pass a null id. Fix: call model.setId(myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()) after creating the model.

issues.descricao: Creating recovery codes in external storage does not remove a previously stored local recovery-codes credential, and validation falls back to local storage, so the replaced codes still authenticate.

comentarios.texto: Successful recovery-code creation in external storage leaves any existing locally stored recovery-code credential active. For a federated user who previously stored codes locally and now has an external provider supporting this type, regeneration no longer calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential's replacement cleanup; UserCredentialManager.isValid falls back to the local validator when external validation rejects an old code, so the supposedly replaced codes still authenticate. Remove the previous local recovery-code credential after successful external creation.

issues.descricao: Exhausted recovery codes are removed with removeStoredCredentialById, which only covers local storage, so a federated recovery-codes credential is never removed.

comentarios.texto: RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() can now return a credential from user storage (federated), but this code still calls removeStoredCredentialById() on it once all codes are used. That removal only targets local stored credentials, so a federated credential may not be removed. The user could then be left with an exhausted credential in user storage. Remove federated credentials through the federated path, or confirm the removal reaches user storage.

RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a credential from user storage, but exhausted codes are cleaned up with removeStoredCredentialById, which only targets the local DB. For a federated credential (possibly with a null id), the exhausted credential is never removed or the call misbehaves, so the user keeps a dead credential. Remove federated credentials through a path that covers user storage, for example by checking where the credential came from.

RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can now return a federated credential. The authenticator still removes an exhausted one with removeStoredCredentialById(getId()), which only deletes from the local store, and the federated model's id may be null. Remove the credential through the path that matches where it was found, for example by checking whether it came from the federated stream and using the federated removal.

issues.descricao: Looking up recovery codes now always queries the federated provider first, which for LDAP users adds an LDAP round-trip and can throw IllegalStateException, failing recovery-code login with a 500.
An error log in the test user storage hard-codes the credential type as 'recovery-codes' instead of using RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE ('recovery-authn-codes').

The test federation provider BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage regenerates the recovery-codes model from the raw list on every getCredentials and never records consumed codes, so the next-code number and allCodesUsed() never reflect usage for its users.

sugestoes.texto: Existing buffers use Redis SETs under the same `span-buf:s:` keys, so deploying this code against buffered data makes `zadd` and `zscan` fail with WRONGTYPE rather than ingesting or flushing those segments. Migrate the existing values or use a versioned key namespace with a compatible drain path before switching their Redis type.

Replaying a span whose original parent redirects to another buffer can put the same payload in both sets, and `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to SUM, replacing its end timestamp with twice that timestamp. Specify `AGGREGATE MAX` in both unions so duplicate delivery cannot promote old spans above newer spans during eviction.

issues.descricao: ZUNIONSTORE merges sorted sets with the default SUM aggregate, so a span payload present in both keys gets a doubled end-timestamp score and is wrongly kept by the oldest-first eviction.

comentarios.texto: ZUNIONSTORE uses AGGREGATE SUM by default, so when the same span payload is present in both `set_key` and the merged `span_key`/`parent_key` (duplicate delivery is anticipated by this buffer's own comments), its score is added instead of being kept equal to `end_timestamp_precise`. Because eviction at line 63 (`zpopmin` by score) compares scores across all members of `set_key`, a summed score makes the duplicated span appear far newer than its real end timestamp and biases eviction away from legitimately-old spans, breaking the stated 'evict oldest end timestamps' contract. Use ZUNIONSTORE ... AGGREGATE MIN (or MAX) so a duplicate keeps a single end timestamp score rather than doubling it.

ZUNIONSTORE uses its default SUM aggregation, so replayed payloads present in both the temporary parent_key and the resolved set_key receive the sum of their end timestamps. Replaying a child whose parent already redirects to an ancestor therefore makes that old span score roughly twice its actual timestamp, protecting it from eviction over genuinely newer spans. Use AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN for identical timestamp scores) on both union operations to preserve timestamp scores when members overlap.

ZUNIONSTORE defaults to AGGREGATE SUM, so a payload present in both the destination and source has its timestamp doubled rather than preserved. This can happen when a previously merged span is replayed into its original subtree key. The duplicated span then sorts after genuinely newer spans and survives ZPOPMIN eviction incorrectly. Specify AGGREGATE MAX (or MIN, since identical payloads should have identical timestamps) on both union calls so merging remains idempotent and scores remain end timestamps.

issues.descricao: Segment keys change from Redis sets to sorted sets under the same key names, so keys left by the previous release make ZADD, ZCARD and ZSCAN fail with WRONGTYPE during rollout, crashing span processing and flushing.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Changed SET ops (scard/sunionstore) to ZSET ops (zcard/zunionstore/zpopmin) with no migration breaks in-flight segments. WHY: Old keys of type SET still live up to TTL; ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZSCAN/ZADD on the opposite type raises WRONGTYPE and fails inserts/flushes during rollout.

The segment keys were migrated from Redis SETs to SORTED SETs (ZADD/ZSCAN/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN), but nothing handles the keys written by the currently deployed release. During a rolling deploy, an existing `span-buf:s:{...}:{id}` key is still a SET, so this `p.zadd(...)` (and the flusher's `p.zscan(...)`, and the Lua `zcard`/`zunionstore`) raises WRONGTYPE 'Operation against a key holding the wrong kind of value'. That exception is unhandled: it aborts the whole pipeline/Lua invocation and crashes the consumer batch. Add a key-schema version to the key name (or a migration/fallback) so old SET-typed keys cannot be touched as sorted sets.

The new ZADD writes sorted sets into the same span-buf:s namespace previously populated by SADD, without migrating existing set keys. During deployment, inserting into an existing buffered segment fails with WRONGTYPE, and the new ZSCAN reader likewise fails on pending old-format segments instead of flushing them. Introduce a coordinated migration/drain or a versioned namespace with compatible handling of pending old-format buffers.

issues.descricao: Claims zpopmin eviction can drop the root span while the has-root flag stays set, flushing a segment without its root.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: zpopmin eviction by lowest end_timestamp has no protection for the segment/root span. WHY: Root with smallest or tied timestamp (tests use identical timestamps, ties break lexicographically) is evicted while hrs flag stays 1, flushing a root-marked segment missing its root.

issues.descricao: max_segment_spans is still a constructor parameter but is no longer enforced; the segment cap is now hardcoded to 1000 in the Lua script, so the configured value is ignored.

comentarios.texto: This hunk removes the only load-time span-count cap (`self.max_segment_spans`): previously a segment exceeding 1001 spans was logged, deleted from `payloads`/`cursors`, and skipped, but now every scanned span is unconditionally appended via `payloads[key].extend(...)`. The new bound relies entirely on insert-time eviction in the Lua script; if that eviction fails to bound a key (e.g. duplicated/scored members or the concurrent-writer case the code itself warns about at lines 457-461), this method will now materialize an unbounded number of spans into memory and emit them, whereas before it was safely skipped. Re-introduce a span-count guard (or verify the invite-time eviction strictly caps cardinality) to keep memory bounded.

buffer.py declares the segment span limit as the configurable `max_segment_spans` (default 1001, line 150) and this hunk removed the `len(payloads[key]) > self.max_segment_spans` size guard from the flush path, while the other changed file (add-buffer.lua line 62) now enforces a hardcoded cap of 1000 spans. The two changed files disagree on what the segment span limit is: the Lua cap (1000) is not the declared `max_segment_spans`, and the buffer no longer applies the declared limit at all. If `max_segment_spans` is configured below 1000 (or below the Lua cap), oversized segments that this code used to skip will now be flushed. Reconcile the constant: either keep/restore the buffer-side guard against `self.max_segment_spans`, or make the Lua cap derive from the same limit instead of hardcoding 1000.

The segment size cap is hardcoded as 1000 here, but SpansBuffer still declares max_segment_spans = 1001 in src/sentry/spans/buffer.py, and this PR deleted the flush-time guard that used that constant. The declared limit and the actually-enforced limit now disagree (and the Python constant is no longer honored anywhere). Make the Lua cap and the Python constant agree — either pass max_segment_spans in as an ARGV instead of the literal 1000, or update the declared constant to 1000 — so the buffer's enforced bound matches the value it declares.

issues.descricao: Tests give every span the same end timestamp and never exceed 1000 spans, so the new score ordering and oldest-first eviction are not tested.

comentarios.texto: All spans in the fixture use identical end_timestamp_precise=1700000000.0, so the ZSET score-dependent behavior (ordering by end time, zunionstore score merge, and Lua zpopmin keeping newest 1000) is neutralised — tests pass even if scores are wrong or eviction keeps the wrong end. Use distinct timestamps and add a >1000-span trimming test asserting oldest evicted.
The missing test for the new trim path (zset ordering/trim by end_timestamp_precise, the >1000-span zpopmin path) is a coverage gap. Add a test that verifies the new trim behavior.

issues.descricao: The span redirect-walk limit was cut from 10000 to 1000 iterations, so trees deeper than 1000 may not resolve to the correct segment root.
The spans buffer module docstring still describes span-buf:s:* keys as plain sets, though they are now sorted sets scored by end_timestamp_precise and trimmed to 1000 spans by add-buffer.lua.
The set_key variable name no longer matches the sorted-set data type after the switch to zadd/zscan.

sugestoes.texto: Each iteration copies the entire accumulated ID list, producing quadratic allocation and copying for large SQLite cleanup batches, including the tens of thousands of orphaned tags created by the new integration test. Build the list with a `strings.Builder` and `strconv.FormatInt` so construction scales linearly with the number of IDs.

The one-minute ticker runs all eight cleanup jobs ten times as often, including `cleanUpTmpFolder`, which enumerates entire directories and reads metadata for every file even when none are expired. Preserve the ten-minute shared cadence, or schedule annotation cleanup separately if it requires a shorter interval.

issues.descricao: Leftover debug logs in the annotation cleanup emit Error-level entries with the full ID list on every batch, flooding error logs during normal operation.
issues.textoGolden: The code uses Error log level for what appears to be debugging information. This will pollute error logs in production. Consider using Debug or Info level instead.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Leftover debug logging calls r.log.Error on every cleanup batch (also duplicated at lines 554-557 and 576-579) dumping full ids slice, cond, and nil err at Error level. WHY: Fires Error-level log per batch and serializes up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize IDs (32767 in new test), spamming error logs/monitoring on every normal cleanup run. HOW: Downgrade to Debug or remove; do not log full ids at Error.

WHAT: Leftover debug logging calls `r.log.Error("Annotations to clean by time", "count", len(ids), "ids", ids, ...)` (and the identical Error-level logs for 'by count' and 'Tags to clean', lines 554/557/576/579) run on every batch in production. WHY: These log the full ID slice (up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize, e.g. 32767 elements) at Error severity on every cleanup iteration, flooding logs with false error noise and large payloads for a normal successful operation, and can trigger error-based alerting. HOW: Remove these log lines, or downgrade to Debug and drop the full `ids` slice (log only the count).

Avoid using Error-level logging on the normal cleanup path. The new r.log.Error calls emit count, ids, cond, and err at lines 534/537, 554/557, and 576/579 during non-error execution, creating log noise; consider downgrading or removing these logs on the normal path.

issues.descricao: The comment states SQLite's parameter limit is 999, which is only true for SQLite versions before 3.32.0.

comentarios.texto: The comment states that SQLite has a parameter limit of 999, but SQLite >= 3.32.0 defaults to 32766 (as the added integration test also recognizes). This branch is choosing a conservative compatibility threshold, not expressing the limit of every SQLite database. Document 999 as the older-version/compatibility threshold so maintainers do not mistake this constant for the actual limit on modern SQLite.

issues.descricao: On MySQL and Postgres, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID without limit, so a cleanup batch size above 65535 makes every DELETE fail.

comentarios.texto: The bind-parameter workaround only handles SQLite's limit; the placeholder branch is used for every other engine with len(ids) placeholders and no bound. The previous implementation had no bind parameters, so this path is new. Postgres (extended protocol) and MySQL both cap bind parameters at 65535, so a configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize larger than that makes this DELETE fail at Exec with a parameter-limit error instead of cleaning anything. Clamp the number of ids per DELETE (e.g. chunk into <=1000/<=65535 id sub-batches) for all dialects, not just SQLite.

On Postgres and MySQL, deleteByIDs binds one placeholder per ID with no cap. A configured AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize above the driver's bind-parameter limit (65535) makes every cleanup batch fail, and the cleanup job then never finishes. Split the IDs into chunks below the limit, or inline the integer IDs as the SQLite branch does.

issues.descricao: The SQLite inline ID list is built with repeated fmt.Sprintf concatenation, which is quadratic in batch size.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: SQLite large-batch IN-list built with repeated fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) in a loop over ids. WHY: Quadratic string copying on large batches (e.g. 32767 IDs in added test) during cleanup, a background job path. HOW: Build with strings.Builder or strings.Join.

The SQLite literal-ID path rebuilds the entire accumulated string for every ID, making SQL construction quadratic in batch size. Large batches explicitly supported by this PR, including the 32,767 setting in the integration test, generate substantial repeated copying and allocation before each delete, consuming cleanup time and memory. Build the list with strings.Builder and append each formatted ID once.

issues.descricao: The cleanup service ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, running every cleanup job ten times as often and increasing database load.
issues.textoGolden: The cleanup job ticker was changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, which can lead to increased database load and contention due to more frequent execution of cleanup tasks. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with performance expectations.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Cleanup ticker changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute with no justification. WHY: Runs all 8 cleanup jobs including the new multi-query (SELECT+DELETE per batch) annotation cleanup 10x more often, multiplying DB load. HOW: Revert to 10 minutes or justify the frequency change separately.

WHAT: The cleanup job ticker interval was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`. WHY: This runs all cleanup jobs (annotations, expired snapshots/versions/images, short URLs, query history) 10× more frequently, multiplying background DB load and lock contention — the opposite of the deadlock mitigation this PR targets — and appears to be a debug leftover unrelated to the described change. HOW: Restore the ticker to `time.Minute * 10`.

The cleanup ticker was changed from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1`, a 10x increase in how often the entire cleanup job runs. This job also drives the annotation/tag cleanup path changed in this PR, which now fetches ID batches into memory and emits Error-level logs per batch, so running it every minute substantially increases DB load and log volume with no functional benefit. Unless a 1-minute cadence is explicitly intended, this should stay at 10 minutes (it reads like a leftover from testing).

issues.descricao: The 'running the max count delete again' test case no longer runs cleanup a second time after the PR's per-subtest seeding and cleanup, so it does not verify that a repeated max-count cleanup deletes nothing.
The annotation cleanup loop stops on a batch whose IDs were already deleted by a concurrent cleaner, leaving the remaining work to the next cycle; checking the fetched count instead would avoid that.
MaxCount annotation cleanup reads victim IDs with LIMIT/OFFSET and deletes them in a separate non-atomic statement, so concurrent deletions can make it delete annotations that should be retained.

sugestoes.texto: When an organization is disabled, `original.isEnabled()` returns false through the organization-aware wrapper, so setting `hideOnLogin` or `linkOnly` makes both predicates false and skips invalidation of a previously populated login list; enabling the organization afterward exposes the hidden or link-only provider because the login bean only rechecks `isEnabled()`. Compare persisted IDP eligibility independently of organization enablement when deciding whether to invalidate the login lists.

issues.descricao: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.textoGolden: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

issues.descricao: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

comentarios.texto: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.descricao: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

comentarios.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.descricao: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.descricao: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

comentarios.texto: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

issues.descricao: The test never consumes or asserts getForLogin's returned providers and never repeats a query, so the cache-hit path that builds the result is untested and could return wrong IDPs without failing.

comentarios.texto: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

issues.descricao: Adding the organization/BROKER_PUBLIC check to the shared LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate also changes IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate, so with organizations disabled a user's linked IdP that has an organizationId but is not public is no longer shown on the login page.
remove() always queries idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias), adding a database lookup on every IDP removal even when the cached entry already holds the model.

sugestoes.texto: Different resource/folder pairs such as `name=a_b, parent=c` and `name=a, parent=b_c` produce the same denial key, so denying the first request makes the second return false without checking its permissions. Encode the key components unambiguously, for example as a JSON array.

issues.descricao: The denial cache key joins name and parent folder with underscores, so different name/parent pairs can collide and a cached denial for one resource denies another until TTL expiry.
issues.textoGolden: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

comentarios.texto: The denial cache key does not distinguish underscores inside resource and parent UIDs from its field separators. For the same namespace, user and action, (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") generate the same key, so denying the first request makes Check return false for the second even if its permissions explicitly allow it. Encode the components unambiguously, for example as a JSON tuple or length-prefixed fields.

The denial cache key is not injective: for the same namespace, user and action, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key. After the first request stores a denial, Check's new early cache return denies the second request without checking its permissions, even if it is allowed. Encode the components unambiguously (for example a JSON tuple or length-prefixed components) and add a test verifying that these two requests do not share a denial entry.

Make the denial-cache key encode component boundaries unambiguously (for example, length-prefix or serialize the components). For the same namespace, user and action, name `a_b` with parent `c` and name `a` with parent `b_c` both produce the suffix `_a_b_c`. Underscores can occur in resource UIDs, so denying the first request caches a key that causes Check to immediately deny the second request without evaluating its permissions, even if that resource is allowed.

issues.descricao: The explicit denial-cache test seeds the cached permission as false instead of true, so it would pass without the denial-cache short-circuit and does not verify it.
issues.textoGolden: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

comentarios.texto: This test claims to prove the permDenialCache short-circuit (service.go:116-121) denies access, but it seeds the cached permission as map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} (a deny), contradicting its comment "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked". Because the cached set is already a deny, checkPermission returns allowed=false, the code falls through to the DB path, and the fake store also returns no permissions, so Allowed stays false. The assertion passes even if the entire permDenialCache early-return were deleted. Seed the cached permission as true (map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": true}) so that only the denial-cache entry can force Allowed=false; otherwise the test does not verify the feature.

The comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked", but the code sets the permCache entry to `false`, which is a deny. The test therefore does not show that the permission cache is skipped. Set the value to `true`, or change the comment to match.

The 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' test would still pass if the permDenialCache check were removed. permCache is seeded with dash1:false, not true as the comment claims, so the normal path also denies. Seed permCache with {"dashboards:uid:dash1": true} and a store that grants the permission, so Allowed=false can only come from the denial entry.

issues.descricao: A cached permission set that denies a resource always triggers a full DB permission reload, so checks over many inaccessible dashboards issue one query per resource instead of being served from cache.

comentarios.texto: Every distinct resource denied by the cached permission map triggers a reload of the entire user's action permission set, because the denial cache is resource-specific and a cached false result always falls through to getIdentityPermissions. Sequential checks of N inaccessible dashboards therefore execute N full permission queries and cache rewrites even with a current action-wide cache; getUserPermissions' singleflight only merges overlapping requests. Bound refreshes per user/action with a short refresh cooldown or generation marker so different resource misses can share a recent refresh.

issues.descricao: The Service struct comment listing its caches was not updated for the new permDenialCache field.

comentarios.texto: The struct doc comment still reads "// Cache for user permissions, user team memberships and user basic roles", but this PR added the new `permDenialCache` field (line 58). The comment no longer enumerates what the struct actually holds and misleads a reader about the new denial-cache field; update it to mention the permission-denial cache so the prose matches the fields.

sugestoes.texto: With a long topic title, the default Ember wrapper emitted by `header-extra-info` becomes a flex item with an automatic content-based minimum width, pushing the navigation beyond the header instead of truncating the title. Apply `min-width: 0` to that direct flex item (or make `.extra-info-wrapper` the component root), so its existing overflow and ellipsis rules can constrain the title.

issues.descricao: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.

comentarios.texto: The flex-item styling targets the inner .extra-info-wrapper rather than the outer div generated by header-extra-info's Ember.Component. With .contents now using flexbox, that outer div retains its automatic minimum width, so a long nowrap topic title cannot shrink to the available space and pushes the navigation panel outside the header instead of being ellipsized by the existing desktop truncation rules. Move the extra-info-wrapper class onto the component's root element and set min-width: 0 on that flex item so ordering and truncation apply to the actual header child.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

comentarios.texto: The alignment mixin does not match the Mozilla fallback emitted by flexbox(): when display: -moz-box is selected, neither align-items nor the WebKit/MS declarations control its cross-axis alignment. Consequently @include align-items(center) in the header and small-action leaves those children at the legacy default instead of vertically centering them. Emit -moz-box-align: $alignment alongside -webkit-box-align so the advertised fallback produces the same alignment.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which never existed in IE/Edge; the legacy property is -ms-flex-align, so the declaration is dead.
issues.textoGolden: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: align-items() mixin emits -ms-align-items: $alignment which is not a valid IE10/11 property (only -ms-flex-align exists). WHY: dead declaration shows wrong contract and leaves IE alignment dependent solely on -ms-flex-align, which also breaks for flex-start/flex-end values. HOW: remove the -ms-align-items line and map flex-start/flex-end to start/end for -ms-flex-align/-webkit-box-align.

issues.descricao: Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.
issues.textoGolden: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

issues.descricao: After .small-action becomes a flex container, float: left on .topic-avatar is dead CSS.

Making .small-action a flex container leaves .small-action-desc content-sized (no flex:1), so the right-floated edit/delete buttons inside it sit right after short action descriptions instead of at the right edge of the row.

On mobile the .small-action custom message keeps margin-left:-40px, tuned for the old 4em left padding; with the new flex layout and 1.5% padding it is pulled into the avatar column and overlaps the icon.

sugestoes.texto: The new interpolation pass expands variable values again when `runQuery` delegates to `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, which still calls `applyTemplateVariables` on every target. A variable whose literal value contains another variable reference (for example, a search value of `$level`) now changes meaning on the second pass; ensure already-interpolated targets bypass downstream template expansion while preserving backend macro handling.

issues.descricao: Loki split/shard queries are now interpolated with applyTemplateVariables before splitting and again on execution, so ad hoc filters are applied twice and already-substituted values are re-interpolated.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables (line 52), but it then delegates each sub-request to runSplitQuery (line 163), which this PR also changed to call datasource.applyTemplateVariables again (querySplitting.ts:299), so each target is interpolated (and ad hoc filters applied) twice. WHY: double interpolation re-runs addAdHocFilters on an already-filtered expression; the stream-selector path masks the duplicate via labelExists() dedup in addFilterToStreamSelector (modifyQuery.ts:494), but parsed/structured-metadata labels use addFilterAsLabelFilter which does not dedup, producing duplicated label filters, and any interpolated value containing '$' can be re-interpolated. This is confirmed by the updated test expecting applyTemplateVariables toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5) for a single target (1 call here + 4 sub-requests through runSplitQuery) instead of 1. HOW: interpolate only once — either remove the interpolation added to runShardSplitQuery and let runSplitQuery do it, or have splitQueriesByStreamShard pass the already-interpolated targets without re-interpolating in runSplitQuery.

The newly interpolated targets are interpolated again by DataSourceWithBackend.query when runQuery executes each split request. TemplateSrv.replace scans the resulting string again, so a variable whose literal value contains another defined variable token (for example, a log-search value containing `$other`) is expanded a second time and produces a different query from the non-splitting path; shard splitting also passes through this additional interpolation. Preserve the early interpolation needed for partitioning while ensuring already-interpolated targets are not interpolated again on execution, and test through the real backend query preparation rather than mocking runQuery.

Targets are interpolated here with `applyTemplateVariables`, including ad hoc filters, and then sent to `datasource.runQuery`, which interpolates them again through the backend path (datasource.ts:324/377). The ad hoc filters may be injected twice, and already-substituted values are re-interpolated, which can produce wrong or invalid LogQL. Interpolate only once. Either clear `scopedVars` and `filters` on the sub-requests after the first pass, or skip interpolation in `runQuery` for already-interpolated requests. The same issue applies to shardQuerySplitting.ts:52.

issues.descricao: runShardSplitQuery now filters empty/hidden targets before interpolation, so an expr that interpolates to an empty string is no longer dropped.

comentarios.texto: The order of operations was inverted relative to the previous contract: interpolation used to run before the `expr`/`hide` filters (interpolateVariablesInQueries(targets).filter(...)), and now the filters run on the *raw* targets before `applyTemplateVariables` is applied. Filtering on the un-interpolated `query.expr` means the previous fallback that dropped a target once variable substitution had emptied its expression no longer exists: a target like `{ expr: '$myVar' }` whose variable resolves to '' is truthy at filter time, survives, is then interpolated to `''`, and is passed into the shard splitting/execution loop as a blank query. To preserve the old contract the filters should run on the interpolated result (or the interpolated expr should be re-checked for emptiness).

sugestoes.texto: Passkey-only users now pass `configuredFor`, but realms using the legacy `keycloak` login theme render the inherited base `login-password.ftl`, which contains only a password form and no passkey controls, leaving those users unable to complete this step. Add the passkeys import and `conditionalUIData` invocation to the base password template as well as the v2 template.

issues.descricao: PasswordForm now accepts passkey-only users, but only the keycloak.v2 login-password.ftl renders the passkeys conditional UI; the base template (used by the legacy keycloak theme) does not, so a passkey-only user is shown a password-only form they cannot complete.

comentarios.texto: PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the active login theme renders the unchanged base login-password.ftl, which contains no passkeys UI. The legacy keycloak theme inherits that template, so a user without a password reaches a password-only challenge with no way to authenticate instead of being able to use the newly accepted passkey credential. Add the passkeys import and conditionalUIData invocation to the base login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

issues.descricao: The comment 'setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled' does not mention that the condition also requires a selected user to own a passkey credential.

comentarios.texto: The new comment says webauthn data is set up "when passkeys enabled", but the guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` also requires that a known/already-selected user actually has a passkey credential. With realm passkeys enabled and a selected user without a passkey, `fillContextForm` is skipped (the test `passwordLogin_reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` relies on exactly this), so the comment misdescribes the condition it documents. Rephrase it to match the code, e.g. "setup webauthn data when conditional passkeys can be used (user unknown or user has a passkey)".

issues.descricao: The test comment says it sets the passwordless policy for discoverable keys, but the updater only disables passkeys for the realm.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'set passwordless policy for discoverable keys' is stale. The updater now only calls setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so it disables passkeys for the realm. Change the comment to say that passkeys are disabled for the realm.

issues.descricao: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys for the realm, so the hidden webauthn form is guaranteed by isPasskeysEnabled() and the new per-user isConfiguredFor check for users without a passkey is never exercised in UsernamePasswordForm.
